chapter: Emmett Hardy, Bix and the Rhythm Kings
title: Chicago union exam, Bix sits in, and Hardy's illness
summary: The Rhythm Kings enlargement at Fry's Inn is ended by the union exam; Hardy teaches Bix his methods, then Hardy falls ill with TB.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And they only stayed a month. Because they got in the, uh, Hardy wasn't in the union. Chink wasn't in the union. I think Skagliona was the only one that was in the union. Well, uh, they had to join the union up there. Well, they had, uh, no, I think, uh, they went to Florida. I think they went to Pensacola or something like that. Where you could join the union for a full five dollars. And join before they went up there. Anyway, they got messed up with the union somehow. Uh, with, uh, Petrillo then was, was, uh, just the head of the Chicago union. And they were working for, for Mike Fritzl and who did it. They was all in with the, uh, Coliseum and the, the gangster era, yeah. And, uh, they, uh, they had to, you had to go take an examination for the union up there. And you had to read. They had a piano player, and you had to read. And Chink couldn't read the note big as his head. Well, Hardy could read, and so could Skagg and Oscar Marco. But Chink couldn't read. So the only, the way they fixed it, the way the gangsters had to fix it, they put, like they had 15 bass players to take the examination, you see. Well, they put Chink at the end of the line. And by the time he got there, he knew. And there he knew.

They had to play the same thing for each one of them, but the only thing was that Chink played it too good. He didn't even put a little bit of his own in there. That wasn't on the paper, you know. And the piano player looked up at him, but anyway they smoothed it. They only worked a month with the Rhythm Kings until the Union threw the four of them out and they came back home. But Bix had come to Chicago in the meantime and he used to come in and ask him to let him sit in. And Paul Moriz and Rapp used to fluff him off, you know. And Emmet did. Emmet told him, I'll let the kid play. And Emmet showed him that third valve business, you see. Bix used it, Hackett uses it. And any, any, any, any, this kid with Welp uses it. And there's a couple guys out on the west coast. You use the third valve instead of the first and second, it's for fast passages. And it gives you a sort of a legato style. And the, and the, the knowledge of the, of the banjo and the guitar and for Bix the piano, and Bobby Hackett the guitar. And he gives, tends to give it that pretty, pretty note style. Yeah. So, uh, like I told you, Rapp and, and, and Paul would, would fluff Bix off and Emmet would. And he showed him everything that he, that he, that was possible for him to show him. Now, Emmet come back and it was right after that. He, he went along around, he played around here a while with Brownlee. And he got sick. And, uh, Harris Shields was on the job with him the night that he got sick. He, he had a, a hemorrhage, you know, and, uh, they were playing over the river somewhere, some high school. And, uh, then he got sick. And he had, he, he went, he went down with TB. You see? Well, he was in bed for, oh, a couple of years. And he beat the, he went over the, over the, over the, over in the Pondy Woods, over there, you know around Manifel and Covington, around there. He stayed over there about a year and a half. And he beat the TB. So, he come home. And, uh, when he came home, well, and I used to go out every day. My mother can tell you, he, uh, if I didn't show up for two o'clock, man, he'd be on the phone wanting to know what's the matter with me, you know. And that was every day. And I'd go out then and I'd ride him around, you know, in the automobile, while he was convalescing. And, uh, then he got, uh, appendicitis hit him. So, they'd rush him to the hospital and, and from being, uh, you know, from laying him in bed all, all, all that time, he was weak. So, he couldn't take a, he couldn't take ether. So, they had to give him a local anesthetic. Otherwise, he'd lay it down watching him because he'd cut his guts open. You see? And, uh, he went through that.
